ble.notes: Two usable signals: the "Flower care"/"Flower mate" local name (the RoPot advertises as "ropot", so a Flower-prefix filter misses it) and the 0xFE95 MiBeacon service data. MiBeacon product ID 0x0098 identifies the plant monitor; the MAC OUI is C4:7C:8D.

mac_prefixes.notes: IEEE subdivided C4:7C:8D into fifteen 28-bit MA-M assignments held by unrelated companies. C4:7C:8D:6 is the one issued to HHCC Plant Technology Co.,Ltd. — the OEM behind the HHCCJCY01 model number — and it is theirs alone, so a match on the full 28 bits names the vendor rather than the octet's fifteen tenants.
The enclosing 24-bit block, kept so a consumer that only understands whole octets still ranks the device. It matches the other fourteen MA-M holders too, which is why it stays at low.

device.manufacturer: Xiaomi / HHCC Plant Technology Co., Ltd.
device.name: Xiaomi Mi Flora Plant Sensor
device.notes:
Plant/soil sensor measuring soil moisture (%), temperature (°C), light intensity (lux), and soil conductivity/fertility (µS/cm). Coin cell (CR2032) powered, ~1 year battery life. $12-17.
PROTOCOL: the device broadcasts Xiaomi MiBeacon service data (16-bit service UUID 0xFE95, product ID 0x0098), so discovery CAN filter on fe95. In connect mode the miflora library (github.com/basnijholt/miflora) reads fixed ATT handles. The known handles are:
  0x03 — Device Name (read)
  0x33 — Mode Change (write): send 0xA01F to enable real-time sensor mode
  0x35 — Sensor Data (read): 16 bytes, LE-encoded
  0x38 — Firmware Version + Battery (read): byte[0]=battery%, bytes[2:]=FW version string
  0x3C — History Read (read): 16-byte entries
  0x3E — History Control (write): 0xA00000 init, 0xA20000 success, 0xA30000 failed
  0x41 — Device Time (read): 4-byte LE uint32 seconds

PASSIVE BROADCAST PATH: roughly once a minute the device emits unencrypted MiBeacon frames carrying temperature, moisture, conductivity and illuminance (and battery on firmware older than 3.2.1) — readable without ever connecting, which is the path ESPHome xiaomi_hhccjcy01, Home Assistant xiaomi_ble and ble_monitor use. Firmware older than ~2.7 only broadcasts its MAC and needs an app-driven firmware update first.
HARDWARE/FAMILY: Dialog DA14580 BLE SoC with an unpopulated SWD header on the PCB; MAC OUI C4:7C:8D. Family: HHCCJCY01 (this device, CR2032), HHCCJCY09 Flower Care Max (Li-Po, advertises "Grow care garden"), HHCCJCY10 (Tuya variant, advertises "TY" with 0xFD50 Tuya service data — a different protocol), HHCCPOT002 (RoPot); the black Flower Care has no Bluetooth at all. The Flower Care vendor app parses a 16-bit product ID from the MiBeacon advertisement and recognizes 152 = 0x0098 (this device), 349 = 0x015D (RoPot) plus two more family members: 956 (a Grow Care plant monitor) and 957 (a thermometer variant); 956/957 are app-derived and not hardware-verified (medium confidence).
SENSOR DATA (handle 0x35, 16 bytes, little-endian):
  bytes 0-1: temperature in 0.1°C (int16 LE)
  byte 2: unknown
  bytes 3-6: light intensity in lux (uint32 LE)
  byte 7: soil moisture in % (0-100)
  bytes 8-9: soil conductivity in µS/cm (uint16 LE)
  bytes 10-15: unknown

FIRMWARE ≥2.6.6: requires writing 0xA01F to handle 0x33 before each read to switch the sensor into real-time mode. Older firmware reads handle 0x35 directly.
HISTORY: hourly measurements are stored on device. History entries (16 bytes each): bytes 0-3=device_time(seconds LE), bytes 4-5=temp(LE, ones-complement for negative), bytes 7-9=light(LE), byte 11=moisture, bytes 12-13=conductivity(LE).
Ropot variant: 24-byte sensor data — no light sensor.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for handles, sensor data encoding, mode-change command, firmware-version parsing and history format — sourced from the miflora library source code in production use across Home Assistant and other integrations. The Flower Care vendor app independently confirms the headline UUIDs (service 0x1204 with 0x1A00/0x1A01/0x1A02; history characteristics 0x1A10/0x1A11/0x1A12), the history commands (0xA00000/0xA1/0xA20000/0xA30000), the sensor data layout and product ID 0x0098. Advertised names "Flower care" / "Flower mate" are community-documented.

factory_reset.effect: Clears paired device state. Battery removal also clears active connection.

steps.action: Remove CR2032 battery for 10+ seconds, then reinsert.

methods.description: Scan for "Flower care" / "Flower mate" advertisement, connect via MAC address, write 0xA01F to handle 0x33 (fw≥2.6.6), read handle 0x35 for sensor data, disconnect.

steps.action: Scan for Flower care / Flower mate BLE advertisement.
Connect and read sensor data via documented handles.

setup.notes: No provisioning or pairing — read-only sensor. Connect and read handles directly. No bonding required for data reads. Firmware update (OTA) is Dialog SPOTA over service 0xFEF5 with the standard SPOTA characteristics, driven by plain unbonded GATT notify/write — no bonding; the app even removes any stale OS-level bond before connecting (vendor app; app-derived, not hardware-verified: medium confidence). This corroborates the DA14580 hardware hypothesis.

rejoin.notes: No persistent pairing. Any central can connect and read.

variants.notes: Advertises under the name "ropot" — a "Flower" prefix filter misses it — while its GATT device name (handle 0x03) reads "Flower care". Sensor data on handle 0x35 is 24 bytes per the miflora library, but WatchFlower observed a 10-byte real-time frame on HHCCPOT002 fw 1.1.5; both layouts exist in the wild. Parsing differs from HHCCJCY01: no light field. temp is still bytes 0-1 (LE int16), moisture at byte 7, conductivity at bytes 8-9.

characteristics.name: Sensor Data
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x35. Returns 16 (or 24 for Ropot) bytes of sensor data, little-endian encoded. Must first write 0xA01F to handle 0x33 (mode change) on firmware ≥2.6.6 to enable real-time mode. Notifications are available: writing 0x0100 to handle 0x36 (this characteristic's CCCD) subscribes to sensor value notifications (Warsaw Hackerspace wiki). The vendor app parses the light value as 24-bit from bytes 3-5, ignoring byte 6 (consistent with the uint32 layout below — byte 6 is effectively unused), and accepts any frame of 10+ bytes.

disable_realtime.description: Disable real-time sensor read mode (counterpart to 0xA01F; sent by the vendor app on disconnect).

serial_number_read.description: Switch handle 0x35 into serial-number read mode; read 0x35 afterwards for the 16-byte serial number.

characteristics.name: Mode Change
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x33. Write 0xA01F to enable real-time sensor mode (required for firmware ≥2.6.6) and 0xC01F to disable it again (vendor app; the app disables realtime mode when it disconnects). Write 0xFDFF to blink the top LED once. Write 0xB0FF to switch handle 0x35 into serial-number read mode (ChrisScheffler wiki); the vendor app confirms this and reads a 16-byte serial (32 hex chars) from handle 0x35 afterwards. Older firmware does not need the mode-change write.

characteristics.name: Firmware Version + Battery
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x38. Returns variable-length data. byte[0] = battery percentage (0-100). bytes[2:] = firmware version string (ASCII). This is the ONLY battery source: no standard Battery Service 0x180F/0x2A19 is present — two independent GATT enumerations (WatchFlower, vrachieru) list only 0x1800, 0xFE95 and 0x1204 (+0x1206).

history_clear.advanced_reason: Permanently deletes all historical data from device storage with no recovery.
history_clear.description: Clear all stored history data on device. IRREVERSIBLE.

history_read_fail.description: Signal that history synchronization failed (sent by the vendor app on sync failure).

characteristics.name: History Control
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x3E. Write 0xA00000 to init history read, 0xA20000 to clear history (CONFIRMED), 0xA1+2byte_addr to request a specific history entry index. 0xA30000 is the history-sync-failed acknowledgement: the miflora library defines it but never sends it, while the vendor app DOES send it when a history sync fails (app-derived, not hardware-verified).

characteristics.name: History Read
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x3C. After writing history_read_init to 0x3E, read this handle for history metadata (bytes 0-1 = uint16 LE count). Then for each entry i, write 0xA1 + 2-byte-LE-address to 0x3E, read 0x3C for the 16-byte history entry.

characteristics.name: Device Time
characteristics.notes: ATT handle 0x41. 4-byte little-endian uint32 device time in seconds.

services.name: Xiaomi Mi Flora Proprietary Service
services.notes: The service and characteristic UUIDs are fixed and documented by three independent RE sources (WatchFlower flowercare-ble-api.md, vrachieru/xiaomi-flower-care-api, ChrisScheffler/miflora wiki): service 0x1204 carries 0x1A00 (handle 0x33, mode change), 0x1A01 (0x35, sensor data) and 0x1A02 (0x38, firmware+battery); 0x1A10 (0x3E, history control), 0x1A11 (0x3C, history read) and 0x1A12 (0x41, device time) — WatchFlower places the history characteristics in a separate service 0x1206, vrachieru in 0x1204 — the vendor app sides with WatchFlower: it addresses the history characteristics (and the 0x1A12 RTC) through service 0x1206 (RTC additionally referenced under 0x1205). The miflora library still works by ATT handle, and the handle numbers are: 0x03=name, 0x33=mode_change, 0x35=sensor_data, 0x38=fw_battery, 0x3C=history_read, 0x3E=history_control, 0x41=device_time.
